exclusions.justification: The registry, schema, verifier, documentation, and their literal contract tests necessarily quote every controlled identifier. Their exact path inventory is locked here to prevent the exclusion from growing silently.

detectors.description: Full player-facing project title.
Short project title outside the full title.
Unqualified compact project slug used in repository and technical identities.
Standalone WOC brand or token symbol.
Lowercase woc-prefixed service, installed path, and container asset identities.
Catch-all woc- and woc/ technical namespaces outside dedicated infrastructure files.
Levy Street organization or attribution name.
Claudemoon realm identifier and its visible rendering.
Persistent hidden grant ID derived from the Claudemoon realm name.
Eastbrook player-facing place label.
Lowercase Eastbrook identifiers not proven to be display-only.
Docker service, container, and volume names in the Eastbrook deployment family.
PostgreSQL user, database, and connection identities for Eastbrook.
Installed Eastbrook filesystem root.
Claudium economic balance, purchase, and presentation identifier.
Armory store, weapon-skin ownership, and presentation identifier.
Known localStorage and sessionStorage key families.
Catch-all lowercase woc_ technical identifier family requiring explicit review.
HTTP headers in the x-woc-* namespace.
HTTP routes in the /api/woc/* namespace.
Internal and upstream Claudium HTTP routes.
OAuth endpoints and callbacks whose deployed values must remain coordinated.
Prometheus and client-performance metric names.
Environment variables controlling mint and economic policy.
Code-level constants that define WOC supply and holder-tier economics.
Known environment variables in the WOC and VITE_WOC namespaces.
Uppercase WOC technical constants and protocol markers that are not environment variables.
Electron desktop application identity.
Android application ID, iOS bundle ID, and mobile OAuth identity.
Android Java package directory corresponding to the installed app identity.
Electron protocol scheme registered in package configuration.
Android intent-filter URL scheme.
iOS CFBundle URL scheme.
Installed desktop deep-link protocol.
Electron custom application origin.
Desktop preload bridge and injected application-origin contract.
Public World of ClaudeCraft domain and subdomain family.
Email identities hosted under the project domain.
Levy Street email identities.
Checked-in Solana WOC mint address.
Authored persistent content identifiers declared in simulation content.
Persistent composite world-content identifiers serialized into saves or state.
Derived heroic IDs that become shipped persistent item and content identifiers.
Database and serialized ownership identifiers for Armory weapon skins.
PostgreSQL advisory-lock key encoding the WOC schema namespace.
Web3 wallet-link table and public-key database identities.
Tracked asset filenames carrying a project brand token.

rules.identifier: World of ClaudeCraft and ClaudeCraft display labels
rules.usage: Player-facing title, copy, metadata, and documentation.
risks: Changing copy must not change adjacent technical identifiers.
rules.justification: The detector covers words separated from compact slugs, domains, protocols, storage keys, and application IDs, so this rule is limited to display text.

evidence.description: Authored UI catalog containing the visible project title.

notes: No display text is changed in phase 1B.

rules.usage: Repository coordinates, package metadata, technical examples, and substrings of separately classified identities.
risks: A global replacement would alter domains, application identities, protocols, and installed paths.
rules.justification: The compact spelling is treated as sensitive wherever it occurs; dedicated rules add stricter classifications for known contracts.

evidence.description: Package metadata contains the compact project slug.

uncertainties: Some repository-only occurrences may later be split into a lower-risk documentation rule.

rules.usage: Brand acronym, reward-unit symbol, token label, and technical prefix explanation.
risks: The same symbol is used in economic and non-economic contexts; visual changes cannot be assumed safe.
rules.justification: Economic usage makes the standalone symbol compatibility-sensitive even when a particular occurrence is prose.

evidence.description: Wallet behavior uses the WOC unit and balance contract.

rules.usage: Organization attribution, community role text, and contact identity.
risks: Attribution and trademark obligations must not be inferred or rewritten mechanically.
rules.justification: The repository contains attribution-like and community-role uses, so any change requires ownership and legal review.

evidence.description: Project credits are the attribution source.

uncertainties: This registry does not determine trademark ownership or licensing obligations.

rules.usage: Realm routing, database partition keys, player-visible realm name, and realm-scoped records.
risks: Changing the realm value could split or orphan realm-scoped market, mail, character, and presence data.
rules.justification: server/realm.ts defines the canonical realm and database call sites persist that value.

evidence.description: Canonical realm definition and validation.

notes: A future display alias must remain separate from the stored realm ID.

rules.identifier: Eastbrook and Eastbrook Vale display labels
rules.usage: Player-facing place and deployment documentation label.
risks: Capitalized labels can sit beside lowercase content, database, Docker, and filesystem IDs.
rules.justification: Only the capitalized display spelling is allowed here; lowercase technical forms are classified separately.

evidence.description: Authored world content provides the visible location name.

notes: No label is changed in phase 1B.

rules.usage: Content slugs, deployment names, database examples, filesystem fragments, and test fixtures.
risks: The family mixes saved content IDs with deployment identities and cannot be globally replaced.
rules.justification: Known database, Docker, and path forms receive additional strict rules; the remaining family stays conservative.

evidence.description: Phase 1A audit identifies Eastbrook as a mixed visible and technical family.

uncertainties: Individual lowercase identifiers need ownership review before any later migration plan.

rules.identifier: eastbrook Docker services, containers, and volumes
rules.usage: Docker Compose service, container, and persistent volume identities.
risks: Renaming a volume without a data migration can create an empty database or wiki instance.
rules.justification: Compose names bind operational resources independently of visible branding.

evidence.description: Docker Compose defines the services and named volumes.

rules.usage: PostgreSQL role, database, connection string, backup, and restore commands.
risks: An uncoordinated rename breaks connections, backup restore, and ownership of existing data.
rules.justification: The values name live database resources, not display labels.

evidence.description: Compose configures the PostgreSQL role and database.

rules.usage: Installed application, environment, and operational script root.
risks: Changing the path can break services, update scripts, or persisted host configuration.
rules.justification: Host filesystem paths require a coordinated deployment migration.

evidence.description: Deployment bootstrap installs and operates from this path.

rules.identifier: lowercase woc-prefixed infrastructure names and installed paths
rules.usage: Container entrypoints, installed directories, service assets, and deployment-local technical names.
risks: Renaming a container path or entrypoint without updating every build and deployment consumer breaks startup or asset loading.
rules.justification: Lowercase woc path and service prefixes are infrastructure contracts, not the WOC economic symbol.

evidence.description: MediaWiki image installs woc-prefixed entrypoints, paths, and branded asset destinations.

rules.usage: Purchased balance, proxy integration, UI unit, routes, database fields, and tests.
risks: A rename can desynchronize balances, checkout, receipts, APIs, and stored values.
rules.justification: Claudium represents a balance-bearing economic concept and is not merely UI copy.

evidence.description: Server economic service owns Claudium balance behavior.

rules.usage: Weapon-skin storefront, account-wide purchases, ownership, loadout, and presentation.
risks: Treating Armory as display-only could disconnect purchased ownership from the store and loadout flows.
rules.justification: Armory participates in account-wide economic ownership and requires domain review before change.

evidence.description: Store view binds Armory presentation to purchase and ownership state.

rules.usage: Browser localStorage and sessionStorage keys for sessions, settings, layouts, editor drafts, and client state.
risks: Renaming a key directly loses sessions, settings, drafts, layout, or onboarding state for existing clients.
rules.justification: The keys are read from previously installed browser state and require an overlap window for migration.

evidence.description: Client settings persist through a woc_* storage key.

notes: A later migration should define per-key aliases and retirement criteria.

rules.usage: Catch-all family spanning storage, SQL fields, functions, metrics, assets, automation, and fixtures.
risks: The prefix spans unrelated compatibility domains and is unsafe for global replacement.
rules.justification: Dedicated rules pin known storage, metric, and economic members while this detector prevents less visible members from escaping review.

evidence.description: Phase 1A audit documents the cross-cutting woc_* namespace.

uncertainties: Remaining family members need finer ownership classification before a future migration.

rules.identifier: woc- and woc/ delimited technical namespaces
rules.usage: Build plugin names, MIME types, CSS and DOM contracts, tooling IDs, agent names, routes, headers, and other delimited technical prefixes.
risks: Delimited WOC prefixes span build, network, UI, tooling, and local protocol contracts that need separate owners.
rules.justification: Dedicated network and infrastructure rules provide stricter classifications while this catch-all prevents remaining woc- and woc/ prefixes from becoming invisible.

evidence.description: Vite plugins use stable woc-prefixed technical names.

uncertainties: Individual families need narrower categories before any later migration.

rules.usage: Secret authentication, editor tooling, and network request metadata.
risks: Changing one side of a header contract breaks authentication or protected tooling requests.
rules.justification: Headers are wire contracts shared by separately deployed clients and services.

evidence.description: Discord bot sends a secret x-woc-* header to the game server.

rules.usage: Client and server balance routes in the WOC namespace.
risks: Changing the route without an alias breaks deployed clients and monitoring.
rules.justification: The route is a public network contract and remains unchanged in this phase.

evidence.description: Wallet server implements the balance route.

rules.usage: Internal and upstream balance, checkout, and economy transport.
risks: Route drift breaks the proxy, SDK, or deployed client independently of display branding.
rules.justification: These are transport contracts for the Claudium economic system.

evidence.description: Server proxy maps Claudium network endpoints.

rules.usage: Discord, GitHub, desktop, mobile, and device authorization endpoints and callback paths.
risks: Provider consoles, applications, and deployed clients must accept both callbacks during transition.
rules.justification: OAuth path changes require coordinated allowlists and a compatibility window.

evidence.description: Authentication server defines OAuth routes and callbacks.

rules.usage: Prometheus series and client performance telemetry names.
risks: Renaming series breaks dashboards, alerts, and historical continuity.
rules.justification: Metric names are external observability contracts even when not player-visible.

evidence.description: Game metrics endpoint emits the woc_* metric family.

rules.identifier: WOC mint and economy environment variables
rules.usage: Mint selection, economy tuning, reward valuation, and client exposure of economic configuration.
risks: Changing names or meanings can alter economic policy or select a different asset.
rules.justification: These variables control economic behavior and require more than an infrastructure-only rename.

evidence.description: Example environment documents economic variable contracts.

rules.usage: Token-supply normalization and holder-tier threshold definitions.
risks: Changing these identities or their meaning can desynchronize server and client economic classification.
rules.justification: These are code-level economic contracts, not environment variables or display labels.

evidence.description: Shared holder-tier logic defines the supply and ordered tier contract.

rules.usage: Build, runtime, service, test, and tooling configuration.
risks: Renaming a variable without simultaneous deployment updates silently changes defaults or disables features.
rules.justification: Environment variable names are deployment interfaces and must not follow display rebranding automatically.

evidence.description: Example environment enumerates deployed configuration names.

rules.usage: Code constants, telemetry symbols, test protocol markers, and other uppercase WOC namespaces not proven to be environment variables.
risks: The uppercase namespace contains several unrelated technical contracts and cannot be rebranded globally.
rules.justification: A controlled environment-variable allowlist separates deployed configuration from other uppercase technical names.

evidence.description: The transformation audit identifies WOC-prefixed technical families as compatibility-sensitive.

uncertainties: Each remaining uppercase family needs ownership review before a future migration.

rules.usage: Electron appId, packaging identity, installed application, updater, and platform integration tests.
risks: A new appId installs as a different application and can break updates, credentials, shortcuts, and platform state.
rules.justification: The appId is an installed application identity independent of the visible product name.

evidence.description: Desktop configuration defines the canonical appId.

rules.identifier: com.worldofclaudecraft mobile application and OAuth IDs
rules.usage: Android application ID and package path, iOS bundle ID, and mobile OAuth callback identity.
risks: Changing a mobile identity produces a different installed app and invalidates store, signing, keychain, and callback configuration.
rules.justification: Mobile application and bundle IDs are platform identities, not visible labels.

evidence.description: Capacitor configuration defines the canonical mobile appId.

rules.usage: Installed deep links, Discord login return, and application navigation.
risks: Existing links and installed protocol handlers continue to target the old scheme.
rules.justification: A protocol transition requires registering and accepting both schemes before retiring the old one.

evidence.description: Desktop config owns the custom protocol.

rules.identifier: worldofclaudecraft installed desktop and mobile URL schemes
rules.usage: Operating-system URL scheme registration for login callbacks and application deep links.
risks: Existing installed applications and callback links continue to depend on the registered scheme.
rules.justification: Application manifests register the raw scheme without ://, so it is a platform protocol contract distinct from a compact project slug.

evidence.description: Android registers the URL scheme and Discord callback host.

notes: A future transition must register both old and new schemes before link producers migrate.

rules.usage: Electron custom origin and server origin allowlist contract.
risks: Origin drift can break desktop API calls or weaken origin validation assumptions.
rules.justification: The origin is coordinated between Electron and server security checks.

evidence.description: Desktop config defines the application origin.

rules.usage: Preload-to-renderer bridge surface and injected API origin.
risks: Changing only preload or renderer breaks the desktop shell at runtime.
rules.justification: The names form a versioned cross-context application protocol.

evidence.description: Electron preload exposes the desktop bridge.

rules.owner: Web, deployment, email, and desktop updates
rules.usage: Public site, dev and admin subdomains, email hosts, OAuth configuration, and Electron update feed.
risks: A domain transition affects DNS, TLS, email, OAuth allowlists, update feeds, links, and origin policy.
rules.justification: Public domains require a redirect and service-coordination plan, never a textual replacement alone.

evidence.description: Desktop update feed allowlist relies on the project domain.

rules.usage: Transactional sender, legal, security, privacy, and support contacts.
risks: Changing an address requires mailbox, sender-authentication, legal-document, and delivery coordination.
rules.justification: Email identities depend on operational infrastructure and public contact continuity.

evidence.description: Transactional email sender is configured under the project domain.

rules.usage: Public contact and attribution addresses.
risks: The repository does not prove mailbox ownership or migration authority.
rules.justification: A future change needs explicit authorization and continuity planning for third-party email identities.

evidence.description: Public security contact is a checked-in email identity.

uncertainties: Mailbox ownership and forwarding capabilities are outside repository evidence.

rules.usage: Default and configured Solana asset identity for wallet balance reads.
risks: Changing the mint points balance reads at a different on-chain asset and cannot migrate the address by renaming.
rules.justification: A Solana mint is an immutable external asset identity.

evidence.description: Wallet service contains the checked-in default mint.

notes: Any replacement is a new economic asset transition, not a rename.

rules.identifier: authored zone, quest, item, dungeon, delve, deed, mob, recipe, skin, and content IDs
rules.usage: Saved inventory, quests, zone state, deeds, encounters, loot, world objects, and cross-system lookups.
risks: Renaming an authored ID can orphan saved progress, inventory, ownership, or server records.
rules.justification: Character and world state serialize raw content identifiers and restore them through authored lookup tables.

evidence.description: Persistent character state contains raw item, quest, zone, and content IDs.

notes: Visible names may change separately while the stored ID remains stable.

rules.usage: Account-wide weapon-skin ownership table and serialized ownership or loadout fields.
risks: Schema or serialized-field drift can hide purchased cosmetics or overwrite active loadouts.
rules.justification: These identifiers bridge database ownership, server state, client state, and economic purchase behavior.

evidence.description: Database schema and queries persist account weapon cosmetics.

rules.usage: Cross-process PostgreSQL advisory lock for schema initialization.
risks: Changing the key can let old and new processes acquire different schema locks during a rolling deployment.
rules.justification: The numeric key is a database coordination identity and encodes WOC even though it is not a visible string.

evidence.description: Database startup uses the advisory-lock key around schema work.

rules.usage: Persistent account-to-wallet association and unique Solana public-key lookup.
risks: Changing the table or column without coordinated DDL and query migration breaks wallet ownership lookup.
rules.justification: The table and public-key column persist the external wallet identity used by economic behavior.

evidence.description: Database DDL and queries persist wallet links by public key.

rules.usage: Tracked logos, icons, screenshots, and distribution images whose filenames carry old branding.
risks: Replacing or renaming files requires updating every manifest and runtime reference without editing generated assets by hand.
rules.justification: Asset names are inventory only in phase 1B; no asset bytes or references are changed.

evidence.description: Phase 1A asset provenance documents the source and generated mirror model.

notes: Future replacement must follow the asset provenance registry and generators.

rules.identifier: generated mirrors of registered sensitive identifiers
rules.usage: Generated UI catalogs, guide data, sitemap, parity goldens, server fixture mirrors, and shipped content-ID golden.
risks: Editing a mirror hides the authored source and the next regeneration will overwrite the change.
rules.justification: Generated occurrences are tracked as mirrors and must have a same-detector authored source occurrence.

evidence.description: Guide instructions identify content.generated.ts as generated from simulation sources.

notes: The verifier rejects a generated-only detector without a linked source rule.
